title: A Debt for the Asset
premise: Ada Eastwick, a veteran financial-crimes investigator, receives calls on a burner phone from her presumed-dead former partner and lover, Elias Vann, who vanished fifteen years ago after a case that cost them everything. Elias is alive inside Meridian Trust, the laundering network Ada has spent a decade failing to crack, and he claims the only way to expose it before an international anti-corruption summit is to surrender the one secret he knows she's kept: the ledger proving Ada herself once laundered money to save her sister's life. As the summit nears, Ada must decide whether to burn her own career and identity to bring down Meridian — trading her secret to Elias, who may be a double agent. In the end, Ada testifies at the summit using the ledger as leverage, Meridian collapses, and Elias dies buying her the minutes she needs; Ada walks away stripped of rank but finally honest, carrying his memory instead of her secret.
about_author: Yara Whitlock is a former compliance auditor who spent eight years tracing illicit money flows across European banks before turning to fiction full-time. She writes thrillers about people trapped between the systems they serve and the truths they bury.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Ada. A routine audit of clean money at Halden & Roe turns strange when Ada finds an account funded by a burner number she recognizes from a fifteen-year-old case file. The beat is quiet unease — the past surfacing in decimal points.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Ada, flashback-woven. We learn how Ada built her reputation on rules after Elias Vann disappeared mid-investigation into Meridian Trust, and how she buried the ledger proving her own crime. Beat: guilt dressed as discipline.

chapters.title: First Ring
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At midnight the burner phone rings; the voice is unmistakably Elias, alive, asking for eleven days of her trust. She traces nothing, tells no one. Beat: vertigo — grief reanimated.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Elias explains Meridian will move its master fund through the summit's host bank in eleven days; exposure requires someone inside, and the price of his cooperation is her secret ledger. Beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: Sister's Interest
chapters.summary: POV Ada, deep flashback. The origin of the ledger: nineteen-year-old Ada laundering a cartel payment to pay for her sister Nadia's surgery. Beat: compassion weaponized against herself.

chapters.title: Internal Affairs Smells Smoke
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Her supervisor, Deputy Director Corliss, notices the anomalous account and assigns a junior analyst, Priya Nair, to shadow Ada. Beat: paranoia entering the office.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at the Fish Market
chapters.summary: POV Ada. First physical meet with Elias since his 'death'; he looks older, guarded, flanked by watchers. He returns her old case notebook — with pages she never wrote. Beat: love and suspicion entangled.

chapters.title: Pages She Never Wrote
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The forged notebook entries suggest Ada was Meridian's mole all along — a frame already built years ago. Beat: realizing someone has been curating her guilt for over a decade.

chapters.title: Priya Follows the Money
chapters.summary: POV Priya Nair. The sharp junior analyst maps the burner number to a shell company chain and grows suspicious of Ada's stonewalling. Beat: ambition colliding with loyalty.

chapters.title: Corliss's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Corliss privately offers Ada immunity if she'll testify that Elias is alive and corrupt — revealing the agency has known for years. Beat: the institution showing its teeth.

chapters.title: Meridian's Cleaner
chapters.summary: POV antagonist — Sable Renner, Meridian's fixer, introduced arranging the summit fund transfer and ordering surveillance on both Ada and Elias. Beat: cold competence, stakes made visceral.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Countdown structure begins; Ada and Elias reconstruct the transfer route from old files, intimacy flickering back through tradecraft. Beat: love against duty, reignited.

chapters.title: Nadia Calls
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Her sister, now healthy and unaware, invites her to dinner; Ada nearly confesses everything and can't. Beat: the human cost of the buried secret.

chapters.title: The Account That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya discovers the framed evidence trail against Ada predates the original case — someone inside the agency built it. Beat: ally conversion through evidence.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Hiding with Elias, they audit each other's lies; he admits he faked his death to infiltrate Meridian after being blackmailed with HER ledger. Beat: betrayal reframed as protection.

chapters.title: Renner Closes a Door
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable burns a Meridian accountant who got curious, sending Ada photographs of the scene as a message. Beat: dread escalating to terror.

chapters.title: The Summit Guest List
chapters.summary: POV Ada. They identify which delegate's bank hosts the master fund — and that Corliss sits on the summit's security committee. Beat: the conspiracy widening upward.

chapters.title: Burner Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Elias (first time). His interiority: fifteen years undercover, loving Ada from a distance, genuinely unsure whether he's protecting her or delivering her. Beat: divided heart.

chapters.title: Immunity Papers
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Corliss pressures Ada to sign testimony naming Elias; signing would trigger Meridian's kill order via leaked schedules. Beat: every door leads somewhere fatal.

chapters.title: Halfway Point: The Vault Key
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Elias reveals the final piece: exposing Meridian requires the vault key held by its founder, Aurel Kastel, accessible only during the summit gala. Beat: plan crystallizing, odds worsening.

chapters.title: Dinner With Nadia
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Second attempt at confession; Nadia reveals she's always known something saved her life and never asked what it cost. Beat: grace without absolution.

chapters.title: Sable's Recruitment
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable approaches Ada directly, offering to make the frame disappear if Ada hands over Elias. Beat: temptation with a professional smile.

chapters.title: The Ledger Decision
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Alone, Ada rereads the ledger — proof she laundered to save Nadia — and decides to trade it to Elias as planned, accepting her own destruction. Beat: the theme made choice.

chapters.title: Handover
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Ada gives him the ledger; he realizes too late that Sable's people tailed the exchange. Beat: tenderness interrupted by gunfire-adjacent panic.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Elias is taken by Meridian; Ada escapes with half the plan and a bleeding hand. Beat: despair, then resolve hardening into steel.

chapters.title: Priya Goes Rogue
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya chooses Ada over the agency, smuggling out the summit security schedule. Beat: the institutional believer breaking faith.

chapters.title: Interrogation Room, Off the Books
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Sable interrogates Elias with the ledger in hand, offering him his old life back if he confirms Ada is the mole. Beat: endurance and doubt.

chapters.title: Corliss Unmasked
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Evidence shows Corliss built the frame fifteen years ago to protect his own early Meridian payments. Beat: rage with a target.

chapters.title: Two Days Out
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada and Priya plan the gala infiltration: Ada trades her testimony silence to get on the guest list via a delegate's compliance team. Beat: gambler's calm.

chapters.title: Kastel's Handshake
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At the gala, Ada meets Aurel Kastel, who recognizes her name from the old ledger and offers her a place beside him. Beat: seduction of power.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada offers Kastel the ledger's location in exchange for Elias and the vault key window — lying beautifully about what else it contains. Beat: the secret spent as currency.

chapters.title: Elias in the Cage
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Held in a Meridian safe room above the gala venue, Elias works his restraints while refusing to sign the false statement. Beat: love as resistance.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: POV multiple, braided short scenes: Ada prepping, Sable suspicious, Corliss panicking, Priya watching feeds. Beat: coiled spring.

chapters.title: The Transfer Begins
chapters.summary: POV Ada. During the keynote, the master fund starts moving; Ada triggers the freeze she and Priya planted, forcing Kastel to open the vault manually. Beat: action climax ignition.

chapters.title: Vault
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Inside the vault, Ada copies the master records onto the summit's own broadcast system as Kastel's men close in. Beat: triumph under a knife.

chapters.title: What Elias Bought
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Escaped, Elias draws off Sable's shooters through the service corridors, buying Ada the upload minutes, and takes a fatal wound doing it. Beat: sacrifice as love's final act.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The Meridian ledger floods every delegate screen mid-session; Corliss is arrested in the chamber; Kastel vanishes into the crowd. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Under summit inquiry, Ada voluntarily discloses her own fifteen-year-old crime, surrendering her career to authenticate the evidence. Beat: identity rebuilt from truth.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Weeks later: Nadia at her side, Priya promoted, Ada cleared but resigned, holding Elias's returned notebook — this time with pages he truly wrote. Beat: grief with warmth in it.

chapters.title: A Debt Repaid
chapters.summary: POV Ada, coda. On the anniversary, the burner phone rings once — a wrong-number silence or a ghost, unresolved — and Ada lets it go unanswered, walking toward the water. Beat: peace earned, memory kept.
